site.defaultMetaDescription: PhD Student at Florida State University

about.introText: I am a Ph.D. student in the School of Communication at Florida State University (FSU). My research examines how people cognitively and emotionally engage with media and communication technologies, and how that engagement shapes their decisions, social connections, and well-being. I am especially interested in interactive media and AI, and in how these technologies can be designed to support healthier human-technology interaction. Before FSU, I earned an M.A. in Quantitative Methods in the Social Sciences from Columbia University and a B.S. in Advertising from Syracuse University.

education.degree: M.A., Quantitative Methods in the Social Sciences

affiliations.name: Prosocial AI and Communication Technology Lab

research.overview: My research focuses on how interactive media, especially video games and immersive technologies such as VR and AR, influence users’ stress, motivation, and emotional well-being.
research.tagline: My research examines how interactive media shape users’ stress, motivation, and well-being. I study when enjoyable experiences become demanding and how design can support both engagement and restoration.

publications.intro: A collection of peer-reviewed journal articles, conference proceedings, and collaborative research spanning Human-Computer Interaction, Social Computing, and Interactive Media.

photoLab.intro: A collection of visual explorations—moments of symmetry, light, and structured chaos in the built environment and beyond.
